title: Nosebleed
summary: Bleeding from the nose, common in children.
callEmergencyIf: Bleeding lasts more than 15 minutes
Child is having trouble breathing
steps: Have the child sit and lean slightly forward; pinch the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes
Apply a cold pack to the bridge of the nose if needed
watchFor: Repeated or heavy bleeding
Dizziness or fainting

title: Head Injury
summary: Bumps or blows to the head that may cause concussion or worse.
callEmergencyIf: Loss of consciousness or repeated vomiting
Severe drowsiness, confusion, or unequal pupil size
steps: Keep the child still and calm; monitor breathing and responsiveness
Apply a cold pack to any bump to reduce swelling
watchFor: Worsening headache, repeated vomiting, or changes in behavior
Difficulty walking, slurred speech, or seizures

title: Scrapes & Scratches
summary: Minor skin abrasions from falls or contact with rough surfaces.
callEmergencyIf: Deep wound with heavy bleeding
Dirt or debris that cannot be removed easily
steps: Clean gently with soap and water; rinse thoroughly
Apply an antibiotic ointment and cover with a clean bandage
watchFor: Increasing redness, swelling, or pus
Fever or spreading warmth around the wound

title: Eyelid Lesions
summary: Cuts, bumps, or small injuries to the eyelid area.
callEmergencyIf: Vision changes or eye pain
Large cut that may need stitches
steps: Rinse the area gently with clean water; avoid rubbing the eye
Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth for bleeding; seek care for deep cuts
watchFor: Redness, discharge, or worsening swelling
Any change in vision

title: Insect Bites & Stings
summary: Bites or stings from insects that usually cause local pain or swelling.
callEmergencyIf: Signs of anaphylaxis: difficulty breathing, swelling of face or throat
Multiple stings with systemic symptoms
steps: Remove stinger if present; wash area with soap and water
Apply a cold pack and give an antihistamine if appropriate for mild itching
watchFor: Increasing swelling, redness, or spreading warmth
Hives, wheezing, or dizziness

title: Sprains & Twists
summary: Injury to ligaments from twisting or rolling a joint.
callEmergencyIf: Deformity or inability to move the limb
Severe pain or numbness
steps: Use RICE: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation for the injured area
Limit weight-bearing and seek evaluation if pain is severe
watchFor: Increasing pain, swelling, or bruising
Persistent inability to use the joint

title: Foreign Body in Eye
summary: Something stuck in the eye causing irritation or pain.
callEmergencyIf: Object embedded in the eye or vision changes
Severe pain that does not improve
steps: Do not rub the eye; try flushing with clean water or saline
If the object is visible and not embedded, gently remove with a clean, damp cloth
watchFor: Persistent redness, pain, or vision problems
Discharge or inability to open the eye

title: Splinter
summary: Small piece of wood, glass, or metal embedded in the skin.
callEmergencyIf: Splinter is deep, large, or near the eye
Signs of infection develop
steps: Clean the area; use sterilized tweezers to remove the splinter if visible
Wash again and apply an antibiotic ointment and bandage if needed
watchFor: Redness, increasing pain, or pus
Fever or spreading redness

title: Hangnail
summary: Small torn piece of skin at the edge of a fingernail or toenail.
callEmergencyIf: Severe pain, spreading redness, or pus
If the area is very swollen or the child has fever
steps: Trim the loose skin with clean nail clippers; soak in warm water if painful
Apply antibiotic ointment if the area is irritated
watchFor: Increasing redness, swelling, or drainage
Difficulty using the finger or toe

title: Nail Crush Injury
summary: Crushing injury to a fingernail or toenail, often painful and swollen.
callEmergencyIf: Severe bleeding that won't stop
Nail is partially or completely torn off
steps: Elevate and apply gentle pressure to control bleeding; ice to reduce swelling
Clean the area and cover with a sterile dressing; seek care for severe injury
watchFor: Increasing pain, swelling, or signs of infection
Nail bed deformity or persistent numbness

title: Bike/Scooter Injury
summary: Injuries from falls while riding bikes or scooters.
callEmergencyIf: Head injury with loss of consciousness or severe bleeding
Suspected broken bone or inability to move a limb
steps: Stop activity and check for injuries; control bleeding and immobilize suspected fractures
If head injury suspected, monitor closely and seek medical evaluation
watchFor: Worsening pain, swelling, or deformity
Nausea, vomiting, or confusion after a head impact

title: Headache
summary: Pain or pressure in the head; common and usually not serious.
callEmergencyIf: Sudden severe headache unlike any before
Headache with fever, stiff neck, or neurological changes
steps: Have the child rest in a quiet, dark room and offer fluids
Use age-appropriate pain relief per dosing guidance if needed
watchFor: Worsening or persistent headaches, changes in vision
Vomiting, confusion, or weakness

title: Allergies
summary: Immune reactions to foods, pollen, pets, or other triggers.
callEmergencyIf: Signs of anaphylaxis: difficulty breathing, swelling of face or throat
Widespread hives with breathing difficulty
steps: Remove the trigger if possible; give antihistamine for mild symptoms if appropriate
For severe reactions, use epinephrine auto-injector and call 911
watchFor: Progressive swelling, wheezing, or persistent vomiting
Dizziness or fainting

title: Minor Burns
summary: First-degree or small second-degree burns affecting only the top layers of skin.
callEmergencyIf: Burn covers a large area, is deep, or involves face/hands/genitals
Burn from chemicals or electricity
steps: Cool the burn under running cool (not cold) water for 10–20 minutes
Cover with a clean, non-stick dressing and seek care if blistering is extensive
watchFor: Increasing pain, redness, or signs of infection
Blisters that break and become red or oozing

title: Contact Dermatitis / Poison Ivy
summary: Skin reaction from contact with irritants or plants like poison ivy.
callEmergencyIf: Swelling of face or eyes, or signs of infection
Widespread rash or breathing difficulty
steps: Wash the area with soap and water as soon as possible
Apply cool compresses and consider topical steroid or antihistamine for itching
watchFor: Increasing redness, pus, or fever
Rash spreading or severe discomfort

title: Mild Dehydration
summary: Loss of fluids from vomiting, diarrhea, or not drinking enough.
callEmergencyIf: Very little or no urine, extreme lethargy, or dry mouth
Inability to keep fluids down
steps: Offer small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution or clear fluids
Encourage rest and monitor urine output and alertness
watchFor: Decreased urine output, sunken eyes, or persistent vomiting
Dizziness or rapid heartbeat
